subject.title: [Feature]: Unified pairing approval panel for the Mac app (replace serial NSAlerts)

question: Should OpenClaw sponsor a unified macOS pairing approval center now, or keep pairing approvals on the current NSAlert-based path with narrower incremental fixes?
rationale: The request is aligned with security/UX priorities, but it changes a native authorization surface and chooses a new product pattern across node and device pairing, so automation should not pick the permanent UX by itself.

options.title: Sponsor unified center
options.body: Approve a focused Mac app implementation that unifies node/device pending requests, shows trust and access context, and keeps current fast-path auto-approval behavior.

options.title: Narrow to alert improvements
options.body: Keep the current prompter architecture and only add missing metadata or copy improvements to the existing NSAlerts.

options.title: Defer native redesign
options.body: Leave the current shipped pairing UI in place until broader macOS app design priorities are settled.

recommendation.title: Sponsor unified center
recommendation.body: Approve a focused Mac app implementation that unifies node/device pending requests, shows trust and access context, and keeps current fast-path auto-approval behavior.

likelyOwner.reason: steipete owns the issue context and has the strongest recent history on the macOS pairing approval UI.
